(2) Redundant/suspicious guards: (u2, has_door_key & door_open) duplicates (u2, door_open); a reward is attached to an impossible case (has_door_key can be true with door_open, but the guard ordering means that reward line is dead). (3) Ordering sensitivity in u0: if multiple propositions become true in one step (e.g., key dropped fires key_lost, or combined events), the guard enumeration must cover all label combinations; the current set does cover the 2^3 cases via else, but the (u0, blocker_moved & has_door_key & door_open) vs (!blocker_moved...) splits are over-specified — simpler state structure would work, though this alone is not fatal. (4) No regression handling: the task and propositions make blocker_moved non-monotonic (ball can be dropped back in front of the door, making it false again) and door_open could in principle toggle — but relocking is impossible, so only blocker_moved regression matters. The RM never moves backward when blocker_moved turns false, e.g., an agent in u2 that drops the ball back still stays in u2 (harmless there since no reward accrued), but an agent in u3 that drops the ball back into the doorway keeps the 0.2 progress reward with no way to lose it; per task regressions should be explicit. (5) Ordering constraint violation: door_open can occur before blocker_moved is ever observed? No — constraints say door_open implies blocker_moved was true, but the RM treats has_door_key-only (u1) and blocker_moved-only (u2) as alternative paths to u3; door_open cannot occur without both has_door_key and blocker_moved having held, so u1 can never reach u3 in practice (door_open requires blocker_moved), making u1 and its 0.1 reward a reward-hacking sink: the agent gets 0.1 for has_door_key with no path to completion from u1 unless blocker_moved later occurs, which it can — but the transition (u1, blocker_moved) is missing: u1's only exit is (u1, door_open). Since door_open requires blocker_moved, if the agent picks up the key first (u1) and then moves the ball, blocker_moved fires but the RM stays in u1; then door_open fires and it reaches u3 — actually that path works. Recheck: in u1 after blocker_moved, (u1, else) keeps u1; door_open still eventually fires. So (4) is the main issue, but the regressions concern is the decisive one: blocker_moved can become false after u2/u3 is entered (ball dropped back), and door_open cannot regress. The machine lacks explicit regression on blocker_moved, which the task requires given blocker_moved is explicitly a non-latch condition. Fix: add regression transitions dropping progress reward or reverting state when blocker_moved turns false in states that assumed it, and remove dead duplicate transition/reward pairs in u2.

Real problems: (a) Missing key_lost handling: the task 'never do both: pick up the key and clear the ball' means a violating trajectory (agent picks up key, drops it firing key_lost, then picks ball) must NOT be rewarded; more importantly the machine ignores key_lost entirely, so trajectories where the key is picked up then dropped (key_lost) are indistinguishable from clean ones in u1/u3 — u1+door_open->u4 rewards opening the door even after the key was acquired and lost before opening, which the proposition semantics (key_lost: key acquired then lost BEFORE door open) treats as a distinct, potentially penalized pattern. (b) u3 else->u3 without door_open transition: from u3 (both key and ball cleared) the agent can open the door, but there is no (u3, door_open) transition, so door_open in u3 loops to u3 and then target_picked_up in u3 goes nowhere — (u3, else) -> u3 means target_picked_up in u3 never reaches u5, making the task unfinishable from u3 (key first then ball then door). (c) u4 has no has_door_key/key_lost regression handling; dropping the key inside the door room fires key_lost with door_open true, correctly excluded by the event, but a drop of the ball back in front of the door while in u2 (blocker_moved regression) is not modeled — blocker_moved can turn false again, and the else self-loop silently absorbs it; the reviewer requires explicit regressions where the task (avoid doing both) needs them. (d) Ordered transition coverage: no transition from u3 at all besides else self-loop, so reaching u3 dead-ends; u3 must have a door_open transition to a door-open state. (e) Compactness concern: u1 and u2 could merge into u3-equivalent, but that is minor. (f) Reward density: only transition rewards, no shaping; acceptable but the dead-end in u3 makes reward unreachable for the key-first-then-ball order. Fix: add (u3, door_open) -> door-open state, track key_lost regressions, ensure target_picked_up reachable from every progress state.

feedback: The RM must enforce the task 'never do both: pick up the key and clear the ball from the door', but the transitions that enter u5 with a -1.0 reward treat this violation as a terminal goal state (u5 is the FINAL/accepting state for target_picked_up). Making the violation path terminate in the final accepting state is semantically wrong: u5 represents task success, and a violating trace is incorrectly accepted/rewarded as final. Violations should route to an explicit non-accepting penalty state (e.g. a dedicated violating state with an absorbing negative reward), not to u5. Additional issues: (1) States u1 and u2, reached from u0 with reward 0.25, encode 'has_door_key without blocker' and 'blocker without has_door_key' respectively, but the -1.0 reward on (u1, blocker_moved, u5) and (u2, has_door_key, u5) triggers even on legitimate progress — e.g. reaching u1 by picking up the key first is allowed (the key may be picked up first), and later picking up the ball from u1 is a natural, legal sequence that the RM punishes with -1.0 and conflates with the violation. Same for u2: acquiring the key after moving the ball is the canonical solving order yet gets -1.0. The violation signal must distinguish actual joint occurrence (both propositions true in the same valuation) rather than mere sequential occurrence of the two events. (2) Progress rewards are only 0.25/0.5 at key/door events with no dense shaping elsewhere, but more importantly the ordering semantics are inverted relative to the constraints: door_open before blocker_moved or has_door_key cannot occur per environment constraints, so transitions like (u0, door_open, u4) with 0.5 are fine, yet (u1, door_open, u4) with only 0.25 under-rewards reaching door state from a subgoal state while (u0, door_open, u4) gives 0.5 — inconsistent reward scale for the same proposition. (3) Ordered transition coverage: the (u3, else) -> u3 state is unreachable and undeclared-purpose; no transition ever enters u3, so it is dead weight. (4) The else self-loops exist per state, which is good, but the (u1, key_lost & !blocker_moved, u0) regression is fine, whereas (u2, !blocker_moved, u0) punishes regression correctly. (5) FINAL_STATES header is present and u5 is declared — good — but u5 being reached by both success and violation means accepting traces of violating behavior. Restructure so that simultaneous key-holding and ball-cleared (the conjunction, which the environment forbids) yields a distinct absorbing penalty state with negative reward, and success (target_picked_up) from any legal state yields the accepting terminal with +1.
